newsitem.title: USA: CNF Menlo unit to hire 200 for Imation pact.
newsitem.headline: CNF Menlo unit to hire 200 for Imation pact.

text.p: Menlo Logistics, a unit of CNF Transportation Inc, is leasing two buildings and will hire 200 employees to support its contract with Imation Corp, Menlo Chief Executive John Williford said Wednesday.
"This is contract logistics in its fullest form, and it is the future for the logistics industry," Williford said during a conference call with reporters.

Under the contract, Menlo will provide distribution services for Imation's operations in North America, Australia and New Zealand. Menlo will ship raw materials to Imation plants, handle warehousing, inventory and packaging, as well as distribute finished goods and oversee return shipments.
Williford declined to give the value and duration of the contract or the effect on profits. "Right now we're investing," he said.

Menlo's newly leased distribution centers are in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania, and in Kansas City, Missouri. The company will build or lease another distribution center on the West Coast for the contract, said Menlo Vice President of Operations Rick Anchan.

Imation executive John Neidermire said Imation's North American operations generate about half the company's $2.5 billion yearly revenues. Imation, which was spun off from 3M last year, needs distribution contractors for its operations in Europe, Latin America and Asia, and Menlo will be considered, Neidermire said.

Menlo had around $270 million in pro forma revenues in the first three quarters of 1996 for CNF Transportation, which was named Consolidated Freightways Inc before it spun off its long-haul motor carrier business in December.
